avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Strong CYP3A4 inducer reduces trametinib plasma concentrations and therapeutic efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; consider alternative mood support if needed with oncology team approval

avoid_supplements.name: Rifampin
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potent CYP3A4/CYP2C8 inducer significantly decreases trametinib exposure
avoid_supplements.action: Contraindicated; notify prescriber immediately if taking this antibiotic

avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Vitamin E (>400 IU/day)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May increase bleeding risk and potentiate anticoagulant effects; trametinib has cardiovascular toxicity concerns
avoid_supplements.action: Limit to dietary sources; discuss high-dose supplementation with oncology team

caution_supplements.name: Grapefruit seed extract
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild CYP3A4 inhibition may increase trametinib levels marginally
caution_supplements.action: Minimize consumption; if used, monitor for increased side effects

caution_supplements.name: Milk thistle
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have modest CYP3A4 effects; limited clinical data in cancer patients
caution_supplements.action: Use with caution and inform oncology team; monitor for efficacy changes

caution_supplements.name: Turmeric/Curcumin (high-dose)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential CYP3A4 inhibition and antiplatelet effects at high doses
caution_supplements.action: Dietary amounts acceptable; avoid concentrated supplements without team consultation

avoid_foods.name: High-fat meals
avoid_foods.mechanism: Significantly increases trametinib absorption and peak plasma levels, raising toxicity risk
avoid_foods.action: Take trametinib on empty stomach (1 hour before or 2 hours after meals); counsel on consistent dosing schedule

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit and grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition may modestly elevate trametinib concentrations
caution_foods.action: Minimize intake; occasional consumption likely acceptable but discuss frequency with pharmacist

caution_foods.name: Cruciferous vegetables (excessive)
caution_foods.mechanism: High intake may induce CYP enzymes, potentially reducing drug levels
caution_foods.action: Normal dietary consumption is safe; avoid excessive supplementation with cruciferous extracts

monitoring_notes: Monitor for hepatotoxicity, rash, cardiac dysfunction, and signs of reduced efficacy. Counsel patients on consistent empty stomach administration and to report all supplements immediately, as many interact via CYP3A4/CYP2C8 pathways or potentiate cardiovascular/hematologic toxicity.
